protocol: Hand-labelled from the 900px label sheets (gridded for coordinates, clean for colour) and the check overlays, without looking at any algorithm output. blood = blood itself lying on a surface: pooled liquid blood, blood film/smear, clot, or a surface whose red is clearly blood lying on it; specular highlights on wet blood are included. Not blood (unlabelled): intact organs and tissue even when dark red (liver, gallbladder wall, muscle, cut pancreas parenchyma, omentum), vessels seen through the surface, perfused pink/red tissue, shadows, scope vignette, black surround, instruments, sutures, mesh and unsoaked gauze; instruments crossing a pool are cut out of the blood polygon. ignore = regions that cannot be called: blurred pool margins (drawn as keyhole rings around a blood core so ignore never covers blood), maroon regions that could be clot or dark tissue, bruising/staining under intact peritoneum, haemorrhagic infarcted tissue, heavily compressed or oversaturated areas, picture-in-picture insets. Frames with no clear blood get blood=[]; small uncertain spots go to ignore rather than blood. bleeding: none = no blood believed present; stain = staining/smear or small clot (including when the likely stain was placed in ignore); pool = collected blood; active = visible flow now (not observable in any single frame here). The gupta clip is open surgery with badly oversaturated colour, so its likely blood is ignored rather than guessed.
